Shirk involves associating partners with Allah

the death of many Qur'an memorizers in battle
the translation of the Qur'an into Persian
the disagreement between the Quraysh and Ansar

introduce new verses into the Qur'an

The biography of the final narrator
The place where the Hadith was collected

Consensus of qualified Muslim jurists on a legal issue
Agreement of only the four major schools

the personal opinion of an unqualified Muslim
reasoning by analogy from an established ruling

The death of all the Prophet's companions
The immediate conversion of the Quraysh leadership
questions.explanation: Persecution in Makkah and the support offered by the people of Madinah made migration necessary and possible.

questions.text: The agreement between the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) and the Quraysh at Hudaybiyyah is significant mainly because it
options: ended Islam as a political movement
created a period of peace that facilitated the spread of Islam
prevented Muslims from performing Hajj permanently
questions.explanation: The truce created conditions in which peaceful contact increased and Islam spread rapidly.

questions.text: Which factor contributed most directly to the Muslim victory at the Battle of Badr?

Divine support combined with Muslim discipline and determination
The battle took place inside Madinah
questions.explanation: Although outnumbered, the Muslims demonstrated determination and discipline and received divine assistance.

questions.text: The conquest of Makkah demonstrated most clearly the Prophet Muhammad's (SAW) commitment to
options: forcing every conquered person to leave Makkah
questions.explanation: The Prophet's conduct after the conquest emphasized forgiveness and reconciliation rather than widespread revenge.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the contribution of Abu Bakr (RA) to the preservation of the Qur'an?
options: He authorized the first collection of the Qur'an into a compiled manuscript
He translated the Qur'an into Latin
He abolished oral transmission of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr ordered the collection of the Qur'anic material into a single compiled manuscript.

questions.text: Which quality of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) was especially associated with his administration as caliph?
questions.explanation: Umar was widely known for justice, accountability, administrative organization and concern for public welfare.

questions.text: The major historical significance of Uthman ibn Affan's (RA) caliphate in relation to the Qur'an was his
options: replacement of the Qur'an with Hadith
standardization and distribution of official copies
questions.explanation: Uthman commissioned standardized copies and distributed them to major Muslim centers.

questions.text: Which article of faith requires Muslims to believe that Allah has knowledge and control over all events?
questions.explanation: Belief in Qadar includes faith in Allah's knowledge, decree and ultimate control over events.

questions.text: Which of the following is an essential distinction between a prophet and an ordinary religious scholar in Islam?
options: A prophet receives revelation from Allah
A prophet must be a political ruler
A scholar receives a new divine scripture
questions.explanation: Prophets are chosen by Allah and receive revelation, whereas scholars acquire knowledge through learning and scholarship.

questions.text: In Islamic jurisprudence, which source is directly derived from the Qur'an and Sunnah through scholarly reasoning?
questions.explanation: Qiyas uses established principles from Islamic sources to determine rulings for new cases.

questions.text: A Muslim who performs wudu but deliberately leaves out an obligatory component has

water is available but a person dislikes using it
a person wants to shorten every prayer
water is unavailable or its use would cause legitimate harm

questions.text: The central purpose of Salah beyond physical movement is to

serve as a substitute for fasting
questions.explanation: Salah is an act of worship that strengthens remembrance, obedience and submission to Allah.

questions.explanation: Deliberately eating during the prescribed fasting period invalidates the fast.

questions.text: The principal social objective of Zakah is to

support eligible recipients and promote social welfare
questions.explanation: Zakah provides financial support to eligible categories and contributes to social welfare and economic justice.

questions.text: Nisab is important in relation to Zakah because it represents
options: the number of prayers performed annually
the minimum age for giving charity
the minimum qualifying amount of wealth for Zakah
questions.explanation: Nisab is the minimum threshold of qualifying wealth above which Zakah becomes due when other conditions are met.

questions.text: The standing at Arafah is regarded as a central component of Hajj because
options: it is a major obligatory rite of the pilgrimage
it replaces Tawaf around the Ka'bah
it marks the beginning of Ramadan
it is performed only by residents of Makkah
questions.explanation: Standing at Arafah is a central obligatory rite of Hajj and occurs on the ninth day of Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.text: Which lesson is most directly associated with the Prophet's (SAW) treatment of his opponents after the conquest of Makkah?
options: Mercy can be exercised even after attaining victory
Tribal loyalty is more important than justice
questions.explanation: The Prophet's conduct showed that victory should not eliminate compassion, forgiveness and justice.

questions.text: Which of the following best reflects the Islamic principle of honesty in business?
options: Using false weights when competition is strong
Disclosing relevant defects and dealing truthfully
Charging different prices through deliberate deception
questions.explanation: Islamic commercial ethics require honesty, transparency and avoidance of deception.

questions.text: Which practice is most clearly prohibited by Islamic commercial ethics?
options: Deliberately using false weights and measures
questions.explanation: Cheating in weights and measures is expressly condemned because it violates fairness and honesty.

questions.text: The Qur'anic emphasis on kindness to parents is significant because it
options: places respect for parents among important moral duties
removes the need to obey Allah
applies only when parents are wealthy
questions.explanation: Islam strongly emphasizes kindness, respect and good treatment of parents while worship remains exclusively for Allah.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the concept of Ummah in Islam?
options: A political party formed by one tribe
The wider community of Muslims united by faith
A family consisting only of descendants of prophets
A group limited to inhabitants of Makkah
questions.explanation: Ummah refers broadly to the Muslim community united by belief and religious bonds.

options: end of all relations between Muslims and non-Muslims
establishment of an organized Muslim community
transfer of the Ka'bah to Madinah
questions.explanation: The Hijrah enabled Muslims to establish a structured community in Madinah.

questions.explanation: The Muhajirun were the Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madinah for the sake of their faith.

questions.text: The Muslims of Madinah who supported and received the migrants from Makkah were known as
questions.explanation: The Ansar were the helpers of Madinah who supported the Prophet and the Muhajirun.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why the Constitution of Madinah was historically important?
options: It restricted all religious communities to Makkah
It provided a framework for relations among different groups in Madinah
It abolished all forms of political leadership
It required every resident to belong to one tribe
questions.explanation: The Constitution established principles governing relations and responsibilities among the communities of Madinah.

questions.text: Which quality of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) is reflected when he faithfully returned goods entrusted to him?
questions.explanation: Amanah means trustworthiness and includes faithfully fulfilling responsibilities and keeping entrusted property.

questions.explanation: Al-Amin means the trustworthy and reflects the Prophet's reputation for honesty and reliability.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the relationship between the Qur'an and Sunnah in Islamic law?
options: The Sunnah explains and provides practical guidance on the Qur'an
The Sunnah completely replaces the Qur'an
The Qur'an is relevant only when no Hadith exists
questions.explanation: The Sunnah explains, illustrates and complements the guidance contained in the Qur'an.

questions.text: Tafsir is primarily concerned with the
options: interpretation and explanation of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Tafsir is the scholarly interpretation and explanation of Qur'anic verses.

questions.text: Tajwid is important in Qur'anic recitation because it
options: changes the meanings of verses intentionally
replaces Arabic pronunciation with local languages
limits the Qur'an to written transmission
questions.explanation: Tajwid provides rules for accurate pronunciation and proper recitation of the Qur'an.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Islamic social justice?
options: Favoring relatives regardless of their conduct
Denying the poor access to assistance
Allowing the wealthy to disregard contracts
Giving people their rights without unjust discrimination
questions.explanation: Islamic justice requires fairness and protection of people's legitimate rights.

questions.text: Which of the following most accurately describes the Islamic concept of brotherhood?
options: It encourages mutual support and solidarity among believers
It requires Muslims to reject all non-Muslims
It is based solely on blood relationship
It applies only to members of one ethnic group
questions.explanation: Islamic brotherhood emphasizes mutual care, cooperation and solidarity based on faith.

questions.text: The Prophet's Farewell Sermon is particularly important because it emphasized
options: human dignity, justice and the sanctity of people's rights
the superiority of one language over all others
the abolition of all forms of commerce
questions.explanation: The Farewell Sermon stressed important principles concerning justice, human dignity and the protection of rights.

questions.text: Which development contributed significantly to the spread of Islam in West Africa?
options: The disappearance of all trans-Saharan trade
Trans-Saharan trade and the activities of Muslim merchants and scholars
questions.explanation: Trade networks connected West Africa with Muslim regions, while merchants and scholars helped spread Islamic beliefs and learning.

questions.text: Timbuktu became particularly famous in Islamic West African history because it
options: served only as a military fortress
was the birthplace of all the early caliphs
replaced Makkah as the centre of Hajj
developed into a major centre of Islamic learning and scholarship
questions.explanation: Timbuktu became renowned for Islamic scholarship, libraries, manuscript culture and centres of learning.

questions.text: Which of the following would best demonstrate taqwa in everyday life?
options: Avoiding wrongdoing because of consciousness and fear of Allah
Performing worship only when people are watching
Seeking wealth regardless of lawful or unlawful means
Ignoring moral rules when they become inconvenient
questions.explanation: Taqwa involves consciousness of Allah that motivates a person to obey Him and avoid wrongdoing.

questions.text: Which action most directly contradicts the Islamic principle of sincerity in worship?
options: Praying privately to seek Allah's pleasure
Performing worship mainly to gain people's admiration
Giving charity secretly for Allah's sake
Fasting with the intention of obeying Allah
questions.explanation: Seeking people's admiration through worship conflicts with sincerity, since worship should be directed to Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why Islam prohibits bribery?
options: It always reduces the price of goods
It can corrupt justice and give unfair advantage
questions.explanation: Bribery undermines justice by giving an unfair advantage and corrupting proper decision-making.

questions.text: A Muslim who forgives another person despite having the ability to retaliate is demonstrating

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates the Islamic principle of consultation?
options: Seeking advice from qualified people before making an important decision
Allowing only the wealthiest person to decide
Rejecting every opinion except one's own
Making decisions secretly to avoid accountability
questions.explanation: Consultation involves seeking and considering appropriate advice before important decisions.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of Suratul-Fatihah in Muslim worship?
options: It is recited in every unit of the obligatory prayers
It contains the complete details of Islamic inheritance
It was the last surah revealed to the Prophet
It was revealed exclusively after the conquest of Makkah
questions.explanation: Suratul-Fatihah is an essential part of Salah and is recited in each rak'ah of the prayer.

questions.text: What central theological lesson is emphasized by Suratul-Ikhlas?
options: The absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah
The history of the Battle of Badr
questions.explanation: Suratul-Ikhlas emphasizes Allah's absolute oneness, uniqueness and independence.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major lesson derived from Suratul-Ma'un?
options: Faith should be reflected in concern for the needy
Pilgrimage is superior to every other act
questions.explanation: Suratul-Ma'un condemns neglect of the needy and emphasizes that genuine religion must influence conduct.

questions.text: In Qur'anic studies, the distinction between Makki and Madani revelations is primarily based on
options: the language in which each verse was written
the identity of the first reciter
whether the revelation occurred before or after the Hijrah
questions.explanation: The standard classification distinguishes Makki revelations as those before the Hijrah and Madani revelations as those after it.

questions.text: Which feature is more commonly associated with Makki revelations?
options: Strong emphasis on Tawhid, resurrection and accountability
Extensive laws governing warfare between states
Detailed rules for the administration of Madinah
questions.explanation: Makki revelations commonly emphasize faith, Tawhid, resurrection and moral accountability.

questions.text: A major characteristic of Madani revelations is the increased emphasis on
questions.explanation: Madani revelations contain substantial guidance on community life, law, social relations and governance.

questions.text: Which of the following was one of the main functions of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in relation to the Qur'an?
options: To replace its verses with his own opinions
To restrict its teachings to the Quraysh
To explain and demonstrate its teachings through his Sunnah
To prevent his companions from memorizing it
questions.explanation: The Prophet explained the Qur'an and demonstrated its teachings through his words, actions and approvals.

questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes a Hadith Qudsi from an ordinary Hadith?
options: A Hadith Qudsi must be part of the Qur'an
A Hadith Qudsi contains only historical information
A Hadith Qudsi cannot have a chain of transmission
In a Hadith Qudsi, the Prophet reports a meaning attributed to Allah, but it is not Qur'an
questions.explanation: Hadith Qudsi conveys a message attributed to Allah but is distinct from the Qur'an in status and wording.

questions.text: Which condition is most important when assessing whether a Hadith chain is connected?
options: Each narrator must have actually received the report from the preceding narrator
Every narrator must have been a political leader
The Hadith must have been written immediately after revelation
The narrators must all have belonged to one tribe
questions.explanation: A connected chain requires reliable transmission links between successive narrators.

questions.text: Which of the following is a recognized characteristic of a Sahih Hadith?
options: Its chain is connected and its narrators are reliable and accurate
Its content must contradict the Qur'an
It must contain no legal or moral teaching
questions.explanation: A Sahih Hadith meets established conditions concerning the chain, narrator reliability, accuracy and absence of serious defects.

questions.text: Why did early Muslim scholars develop systematic methods for evaluating Hadith narrators?
options: To prevent Muslims from learning Arabic
To distinguish reliable reports from unreliable ones
To make every Hadith identical in wording
questions.explanation: Hadith criticism developed to protect the Sunnah by identifying reliable and unreliable transmissions.

questions.text: Which of the following is most closely associated with Imam al-Bukhari's method of Hadith collection?
options: Applying strict standards to the authenticity of reports
questions.explanation: Imam al-Bukhari was renowned for applying rigorous standards when selecting authentic Hadith.

questions.text: Which of the following represents a proper relationship between Ijma and Qiyas?
options: Both are methods used by scholars in deriving Islamic legal rulings
Both refer exclusively to Qur'anic revelation
Ijma means analogy while Qiyas means consensus
Neither has any relationship with Islamic jurisprudence
questions.explanation: Ijma and Qiyas are recognized juristic tools used in Islamic legal reasoning.

questions.text: The effective cause shared by an original case and a new case in Qiyas is called

questions.text: Which situation provides the strongest basis for applying Qiyas?
options: A matter already explicitly settled by an unambiguous Qur'anic verse
A matter involving no legal principle at all
A new case sharing the relevant effective cause of an established ruling
A disagreement based solely on personal preference
questions.explanation: Qiyas applies when a new case shares the relevant effective cause of an existing legal ruling.

questions.text: Which of the following was a major objective of the Prophet's mission?
options: To establish Quraysh as a permanent ruling class
To abolish all forms of social responsibility
To make wealth the basis of human superiority
To call humanity to worship Allah and live according to divine guidance
questions.explanation: The Prophet's mission centered on Tawhid, moral reform and obedience to Allah's guidance.

questions.text: The persecution suffered by early Muslims in Makkah mainly demonstrated the
options: strength of opposition to the Prophet's message among influential groups
complete acceptance of Islam by the Quraysh
absence of any tribal influence in Makkah
questions.explanation: Many influential Quraysh opposed Islam because they perceived the new faith as threatening their beliefs and established interests.

questions.text: The migration of some Muslims to Abyssinia was significant because it
options: provided persecuted Muslims with temporary protection under a just ruler
ended the Prophet's mission in Makkah
questions.explanation: Muslims sought refuge in Abyssinia because its Christian ruler, the Negus, was known for justice and protection.

questions.text: The acceptance of Islam by the people of Yathrib before the Hijrah contributed directly to
options: the end of all relations with Makkah
the establishment of a supportive Muslim community in Madinah
the cancellation of the Prophet's mission
questions.explanation: The support of the people of Yathrib provided the foundation for the Muslim community that developed in Madinah.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the importance of the Pledges of Aqabah?
options: They established the rules of inheritance
They ended the obligation of Salah
They introduced the compilation of Hadith
They prepared the way for the Prophet's migration and the establishment of the Madinan community
questions.explanation: The pledges involved commitments by people from Yathrib and helped prepare the ground for the Hijrah.

questions.text: The brotherhood established between the Muhajirun and Ansar primarily aimed at
options: strengthening social solidarity and mutual support
creating rivalry between the two groups
separating migrants from the Madinan population
making tribal identity more important than Islam
questions.explanation: The Prophet established bonds between the Muhajirun and Ansar to promote unity, support and social integration.

questions.text: Which principle is demonstrated by the Prophet's (SAW) consultation with his companions on important matters?
questions.explanation: Shura means consultation and is an important principle in Islamic communal affairs.

questions.text: The Battle of Uhud is particularly instructive because the setback suffered by the Muslims highlighted the danger of
options: disobeying strategic instructions and becoming attached to worldly gain
questions.explanation: The events at Uhud demonstrate the consequences of disobedience to the Prophet's instructions and excessive attachment to immediate gains.

questions.text: Which lesson is most appropriate from the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
options: Every compromise is a sign of weakness
Muslims should reject all peaceful agreements
Political agreements have no place in Islam
Patience and strategic restraint can produce greater long-term benefits
questions.explanation: Hudaybiyyah showed that patience and strategic restraint could create conditions favorable to the growth of Islam.

questions.text: The Farewell Pilgrimage is especially associated with the Prophet's (SAW) emphasis on
options: the sanctity of life, property and human dignity
the superiority of one tribe over another
the abolition of all commercial activities
the restriction of Islam to Arabia
questions.explanation: The Farewell Sermon emphasized important principles concerning human dignity, justice and the sanctity of rights.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the role of intention in Islamic acts of worship?
options: Intention is irrelevant if the action is difficult
The intention helps determine the purpose and religious value of an act
Intention can transform an unlawful act into a lawful one
questions.explanation: Niyyah establishes the purpose behind an act and is fundamental to the validity and spiritual value of many acts of worship.

questions.text: Which of the following situations most clearly demonstrates Riya?
options: Praying alone to seek Allah's pleasure
Performing worship to gain admiration from people
Helping a neighbour without seeking recognition
questions.explanation: Riya refers to showing off in worship or performing religious acts for people's admiration.

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes Sabr from passive acceptance of wrongdoing?
options: Sabr requires a person to approve every injustice
Sabr means refusing to take any lawful action
Sabr means abandoning all efforts to solve problems
Sabr involves patient perseverance while remaining within Islamic principles
questions.explanation: Sabr means patience and steadfastness, not approval of wrongdoing or abandonment of lawful efforts.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important spiritual effect of Zakah on the giver?
options: It purifies wealth and helps cultivate generosity
It removes the obligation of Salah
questions.explanation: Zakah purifies wealth and encourages generosity and social responsibility.

questions.text: A Muslim possesses qualifying wealth above the Nisab for the required period. The most appropriate conclusion is that
options: Zakah is due if the other conditions are satisfied
the person must give all the wealth away
the person is exempt from all other obligations
questions.explanation: When the relevant conditions are fulfilled, including reaching Nisab and the applicable holding period, Zakah becomes due.

questions.text: Which of the following best demonstrates the social purpose of Sawm?
options: Removing the need for community life
Developing self-control, empathy and consciousness of Allah
Replacing all other forms of worship
questions.explanation: Fasting develops self-discipline and empathy while strengthening consciousness of Allah.

questions.text: A traveller who finds fasting during Ramadan difficult may be allowed to
options: break the fast and make it up later according to Islamic provisions
questions.explanation: Islam provides concessions for certain travellers, including making up missed obligatory fasts later.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the spiritual significance of Hajj?
options: It demonstrates submission, equality and devotion to Allah
It is primarily a commercial festival
It is restricted to wealthy Arabs
It replaces all other pillars of Islam
questions.explanation: Hajj is an act of devotion that demonstrates submission to Allah and emphasizes the equality of Muslims.

questions.text: The wearing of Ihram during Hajj is significant because it
options: symbolizes entry into the sacred state of pilgrimage
is required only after leaving Makkah
questions.explanation: Ihram is the sacred state entered by pilgrims, accompanied by specific restrictions and acts of worship.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates Ihsan in social relations?
options: Repaying kindness only when there is a benefit
Doing good with excellence even when no reward is expected
Treating people well only when they are wealthy
questions.explanation: Ihsan involves excellence and doing good sincerely, including when there is no immediate worldly benefit.

questions.text: Which action most directly violates the Islamic prohibition of Ghibah?
options: Mentioning an absent person's faults in a way that they would dislike
questions.explanation: Ghibah involves mentioning an absent person's faults in a manner they would dislike, even if the statement is true.

questions.text: Why is backbiting considered particularly harmful to Muslim society?
options: It damages trust and promotes hostility among people
questions.explanation: Backbiting can damage reputations, weaken trust and create hostility within the community.

questions.text: Which of the following is the best Islamic response to discovering that a friend has committed a minor wrong?
options: Offer sincere advice and encourage correction of the wrong
Ignore every wrong regardless of its consequences
questions.explanation: Islam encourages sincere advice and correction while avoiding unnecessary exposure and humiliation.

questions.text: Which principle is most directly violated by a trader who hides a serious defect in a product?
questions.explanation: Concealing important defects deceives the buyer and violates Islamic principles of honesty and fairness.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major reason Islam prohibits Riba?
options: It prevents people from owning property
It makes every form of trade unlawful
It can create unjust financial exploitation and guaranteed gain on certain loans
questions.explanation: Riba is prohibited because it involves forms of unjustified increase and can contribute to exploitation in financial dealings.

questions.text: Which of the following best represents Islamic stewardship of wealth?
options: Recognizing wealth as a trust and using it lawfully and responsibly
Accumulating wealth through any available means
Refusing to assist people in need
Considering wealth more important than religious obligations
questions.explanation: Islam teaches that wealth is a trust and should be acquired and spent through lawful and responsible means.

questions.text: The Islamic principle of equality does not mean that
options: everyone must possess exactly the same amount of wealth
people should not be judged by race or lineage
questions.explanation: Islamic equality emphasizes equal human dignity and justice, not necessarily identical levels of wealth or possessions.

questions.text: Which factor most contributed to the intellectual development of Islamic civilization in West Africa?
options: The complete absence of foreign contact
The closure of centres of learning
The establishment of centres of Islamic learning and scholarship
questions.explanation: Islamic centres of learning, scholars and Arabic literacy played major roles in intellectual development in West Africa.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the historical importance of the Sankore tradition in Timbuktu?
options: It was associated with advanced Islamic learning and scholarship
It served exclusively as a military barracks
It was established as a centre for idol worship
It replaced the Ka'bah as the Islamic centre of pilgrimage
questions.explanation: The Sankore tradition is associated with Timbuktu's reputation as an important centre of Islamic education and scholarship.

questions.text: Which method was particularly important in the early spread of Islam among West African trading communities?
options: Interaction through trade, scholarship and peaceful contact
questions.explanation: Trade and peaceful interaction created opportunities for Muslims to share Islamic beliefs, practices and learning.

questions.text: Which of the following best demonstrates justice in Islamic leadership?
options: Giving relatives preference regardless of wrongdoing
Applying principles of justice even when dealing with people one dislikes
Allowing wealthy citizens to escape all accountability
questions.explanation: Islamic justice requires fairness and impartiality, even toward people with whom one disagrees.

questions.text: Which quality of Abu Bakr (RA) was especially evident when he remained firm after the Prophet's death?
options: Steadfastness and commitment to Islamic principles
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr demonstrated remarkable steadfastness in preserving the unity and obligations of the Muslim community.

questions.text: Which administrative development is strongly associated with Umar ibn al-Khattab's caliphate?
options: Expansion and organization of administrative institutions in the growing Muslim state
questions.explanation: Umar's caliphate saw significant administrative organization as the Muslim state expanded.

questions.text: Which of the following most accurately describes the concept of Ummah?
options: A community based exclusively on blood relations
A community united primarily by Islamic faith and shared religious bonds
A political group limited to one city
A tribe descended from one ancestor
questions.explanation: The Ummah refers to the wider Muslim community united by faith and shared religious identity.

questions.text: Which of the following situations best demonstrates obedience to Allah in everyday life?
options: Ignoring obligations when they become inconvenient
Choosing lawful conduct even when an unlawful alternative appears more profitable
Following personal desires whenever they conflict with Islamic principles
questions.explanation: Obedience to Allah involves choosing lawful and ethical conduct even when wrongdoing appears personally advantageous.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why the Qur'an is regarded as the primary source of Islamic law?
options: It contains every possible detail of every future event
It was written by the companions after the Prophet's death
It applies only to acts of worship
It contains fundamental divine guidance from which Islamic legal principles are derived
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is the primary source of Islamic law because it provides divine guidance and fundamental principles for belief, worship and conduct.

questions.text: Which statement best reflects the Islamic understanding of human accountability?
options: People are responsible for their choices and will be accountable before Allah
Only rulers are accountable before Allah
Wealth determines the degree of accountability
Human beings have no responsibility for their actions
questions.explanation: Islam teaches that individuals are accountable for their choices and deeds before Allah.

questions.text: A Muslim who believes in Qadar should nevertheless continue to make lawful efforts because
options: belief in Qadar removes all moral responsibility
human beings are expected to act responsibly while trusting Allah's decree
effort has no relationship with accountability
questions.explanation: Belief in Qadar does not cancel human responsibility; Muslims are expected to make lawful efforts and trust Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following is the clearest example of Amanah in public office?
options: Using public funds for personal luxury
Giving government contracts only to relatives
Protecting entrusted resources and using them for their proper purpose
Hiding financial records from legitimate oversight
questions.explanation: Amanah requires entrusted responsibilities and resources to be handled honestly and for their intended purpose.

questions.text: Which of the following is most consistent with Islamic conflict resolution?
options: Allowing wealth to determine who is right
questions.explanation: Islam encourages reconciliation while maintaining justice and fairness between disputing parties.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of Tawhid in Islam?
options: It establishes the belief that Allah alone deserves worship
It requires Muslims to reject all forms of social interaction
It makes obedience to prophets unnecessary
It limits worship to acts performed in the mosque
questions.explanation: Tawhid is the belief in the absolute oneness of Allah and that He alone deserves worship.

questions.text: Which attribute of Allah is most directly expressed by the name Al-Ghafur?
questions.explanation: Al-Ghafur means The Most Forgiving, emphasizing Allah's forgiveness of those who sincerely repent.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of sending prophets according to Islamic teachings?
options: To provide worldly wealth to their followers
To convey Allah's guidance and call people to worship Him
To eliminate all differences in human abilities
questions.explanation: Prophets were sent to convey divine guidance, teach people and call them to worship Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major difference between a prophet and an ordinary human being in Islamic belief?
options: A prophet must possess unlimited knowledge
A prophet cannot experience human emotions
A prophet is free from every human need
A prophet receives divine revelation for guidance
questions.explanation: Prophets are human beings chosen by Allah to receive and convey divine revelation.

questions.text: Which prophet is particularly associated with the construction of the Ka'bah together with his son?
questions.explanation: Prophet Ibrahim and his son Isma'il are associated with raising the foundations of the Ka'bah.

questions.text: The story of Prophet Yusuf in the Qur'an strongly demonstrates the importance of
options: patience, forgiveness and trust in Allah
questions.explanation: The story of Yusuf illustrates patience during hardship, forgiveness and reliance upon Allah.

questions.text: What major lesson can be derived from the response of Prophet Musa to Pharaoh's oppression?
options: Faith requires courage in confronting falsehood
Leadership should remain within one family
questions.explanation: The story of Musa demonstrates courage, faith and steadfastness when confronting oppression and falsehood.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Qur'an's treatment of previous prophets?
options: It rejects all prophets before Muhammad
It presents them only as political leaders
It mentions them only in relation to warfare
It confirms the continuity of divine guidance through many prophets
questions.explanation: The Qur'an recognizes many earlier prophets and presents their missions as part of the history of divine guidance.

questions.text: What is the primary significance of Laylat al-Qadr?
options: It is described as a night better than a thousand months
It marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar
It is the day of the Prophet's birth
It is the day when Hajj becomes obligatory
questions.explanation: Laylat al-Qadr is highly significant because the Qur'an describes it as better than a thousand months.

questions.text: Which activity is most appropriate for a Muslim seeking the blessings of Laylat al-Qadr?
options: Engaging in prayer, remembrance and supplication
questions.explanation: Muslims are encouraged to devote Laylat al-Qadr to worship, prayer, remembrance and supplication.

questions.text: Which of the following is the best description of Taqwa?
options: Consciousness of Allah that encourages obedience and avoidance of wrongdoing
questions.explanation: Taqwa involves consciousness and awareness of Allah that guides a person toward obedience and away from wrongdoing.

questions.text: A Muslim who refuses to cheat in an examination despite having an opportunity demonstrates
questions.explanation: Avoiding wrongdoing because of consciousness of Allah is an example of Taqwa.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to strengthen brotherhood among Muslims?
options: Making wealth the basis of friendship
questions.explanation: Mutual respect, cooperation and concern for one another strengthen Islamic brotherhood.

questions.text: What is the Islamic attitude toward parents who are elderly and in need of assistance?
options: Their care should be left entirely to neighbours
They should be treated with kindness and respect
They should be avoided because they are dependent
Their advice should always be rejected
questions.explanation: Islam places strong emphasis on kindness, respect and good treatment of parents, especially when they become elderly.

questions.text: Which of the following actions best illustrates Birr al-Walidayn?
options: Ignoring parents when they need help
Showing kindness and fulfilling lawful responsibilities toward parents
questions.explanation: Birr al-Walidayn means showing dutifulness, kindness and respect toward one's parents.

questions.text: When a Muslim is asked to obey a parent in committing a sinful act, the Islamic principle is that
options: the parent must always be obeyed
obedience is required because parents are superior
sin becomes lawful when requested by a parent
obedience to Allah takes precedence over obedience in sin
questions.explanation: Islam commands kindness to parents but does not require obedience in disobedience to Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Islamic teachings concerning neighbours?
options: Neighbours have rights to good treatment and consideration
Only Muslim neighbours deserve good treatment
A person's responsibility ends at the boundary of the home
questions.explanation: Islam strongly encourages good treatment, consideration and protection of neighbours' rights.

questions.text: Which action is most likely to violate the rights of a neighbour?
options: Deliberately causing repeated disturbance to the neighbour
questions.explanation: Deliberately causing harm or disturbance to a neighbour conflicts with Islamic teachings on neighbourly rights.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major purpose of Islamic marriage?
options: To provide a lawful framework for family life and mutual responsibility
questions.explanation: Marriage in Islam provides a lawful framework for family life, companionship and mutual responsibilities.

questions.text: Which quality is especially important in choosing a spouse according to Islamic principles?
questions.explanation: Islam places strong emphasis on religious commitment and good character when considering marriage.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Islamic concept of Mahr?
options: A mandatory gift or payment given by the husband to the wife as part of the marriage
A tax paid by every married couple to the government
A voluntary donation to the mosque
A payment made by the wife to her husband's relatives
questions.explanation: Mahr is the obligatory marital gift given by the husband to the wife.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key responsibility of parents toward their children?
options: Providing guidance, care and proper upbringing
Allowing children to make every decision without guidance
Teaching children to value wealth above character
Preventing children from learning useful knowledge
questions.explanation: Parents are responsible for caring for their children and providing proper moral and educational guidance.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates Islamic moderation in spending?
options: Avoiding extravagance while meeting legitimate needs
Borrowing unnecessarily to maintain social status
questions.explanation: Islam encourages moderation by avoiding both wastefulness and unreasonable miserliness.

questions.text: The Qur'anic condemnation of Israf primarily concerns
questions.explanation: Israf refers to excessiveness and wastefulness, which Islamic teachings discourage.

questions.text: Which of the following is the clearest example of Shukr?
options: Recognizing Allah's blessings and using them responsibly
Attributing every success solely to oneself
Refusing to acknowledge help received from others
questions.explanation: Shukr means gratitude, including recognizing Allah's blessings and responding to them appropriately.

questions.text: A Muslim who uses knowledge to benefit others while remaining humble demonstrates
options: Shukr and responsible use of knowledge
questions.explanation: Using knowledge beneficially while remaining humble reflects gratitude and responsible conduct.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains Hasad?
options: Giving sincere advice to a friend
Desiring that another person's blessing or advantage be removed
Helping someone who is facing difficulty
questions.explanation: Hasad refers to envy in which a person wishes for another person's blessing or advantage to be removed.

questions.text: Which action is the best way to overcome envy toward a successful person?
options: Trying to damage the person's reputation
Praying for blessings and focusing on one's own lawful efforts
questions.explanation: A healthy response to envy is to seek Allah's blessings, appreciate what one has and pursue lawful efforts.

questions.text: Which of the following is most closely associated with Tawbah?
questions.explanation: Tawbah means sincere repentance and turning back to Allah after wrongdoing.

questions.text: Which condition strengthens the sincerity of Tawbah?
options: Planning to repeat the sin immediately
Feeling genuine remorse and resolving not to return to the wrongdoing
Blaming another person for every mistake
Repenting only when praised by others
questions.explanation: Sincere repentance includes remorse and a genuine resolve to abandon the wrongdoing.

questions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes Tawakkul from laziness?
options: Tawakkul requires abandoning all lawful effort
Tawakkul combines lawful effort with reliance upon Allah
Tawakkul means expecting success without action
questions.explanation: Tawakkul means relying upon Allah while taking appropriate lawful steps toward one's objectives.

questions.text: A student prepares thoroughly for an examination and then trusts Allah with the outcome. This best illustrates
questions.explanation: The student combines responsible effort with reliance upon Allah, which illustrates Tawakkul.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major danger of Takabbur?
options: It can prevent a person from accepting truth and respecting others
questions.explanation: Takabbur, or arrogance, can cause a person to reject truth and look down upon others.

questions.text: Which behaviour is most inconsistent with humility in Islam?
options: Considering oneself superior to others because of wealth
questions.explanation: Considering oneself superior to others because of wealth is a form of arrogance and contradicts Islamic humility.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the Islamic prohibition of lying?
options: Lying is allowed whenever it is convenient
Lying is encouraged in business negotiations
Falsehood damages trust and contradicts truthful conduct
Lying becomes obligatory when a person is wealthy
questions.explanation: Islam strongly encourages truthfulness because lying damages trust and undermines moral integrity.

questions.text: A trader gives accurate information about the quality of goods even when doing so may reduce the sale. This demonstrates
questions.explanation: Sidq means truthfulness, and giving accurate information in business is an example of it.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Islamic concept of Adl?
questions.explanation: Adl refers to justice, fairness and giving people their proper rights.

questions.text: A judge refuses to favour a close relative in a legal dispute. Which Islamic principle is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Refusing to favour a relative and applying justice impartially demonstrates Adl.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important purpose of fasting beyond abstaining from food and drink?
questions.explanation: Fasting develops discipline, restraint and consciousness of Allah in addition to abstention from food and drink.

questions.text: Which of the following acts can invalidate a fast when deliberately performed during the fasting period?
questions.explanation: Deliberately eating or drinking during the prescribed fasting period invalidates the fast.

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the primary objectives of Salah?
options: To establish regular remembrance and worship of Allah
To replace all other forms of good conduct
questions.explanation: Salah is a central act of worship that regularly connects the believer with Allah through remembrance and submission.

questions.text: Why is cleanliness important before performing Salah?
options: Purification is part of the conditions and preparation for prayer
It removes the need for intention
questions.explanation: Purification is an important preparation for Salah and forms part of its conditions.

questions.text: Which of the following is the principal purpose of Wudu?
options: To distinguish one tribe from another
To achieve ritual purification before acts requiring it
To replace the performance of Salah
questions.explanation: Wudu is a prescribed form of ritual purification performed before certain acts of worship, including Salah.

questions.text: When water cannot be used for purification because of a valid circumstance, which alternative may be permitted?
questions.explanation: Tayammum is a form of dry purification permitted under certain circumstances when water cannot appropriately be used.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of congregational Salah?
options: It promotes unity and strengthens communal bonds
It is performed only by wealthy Muslims
It removes the need for individual worship
It is intended mainly for public recognition
questions.explanation: Congregational prayer promotes unity, equality and a sense of community among Muslims.

questions.text: Which statement about the Friday prayer is most accurate?
options: It is performed only during Ramadan
It is a special congregational prayer associated with Friday
It replaces every daily prayer of the week
It is performed only during Hajj
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah is the special congregational Friday prayer accompanied by a sermon.

questions.text: The Khutbah delivered before the Friday prayer primarily serves to
options: replace all forms of Islamic learning
questions.explanation: The Khutbah provides religious guidance, reminders and instruction to the congregation.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the purpose of Zakat in relation to society?
options: To create permanent dependence among the poor
To eliminate all differences in income
To support eligible recipients and promote social welfare
questions.explanation: Zakat supports eligible recipients and contributes to social welfare and economic responsibility.

questions.text: Which category of people is among those eligible to receive Zakat?
questions.explanation: The poor and needy are among the categories of people identified as eligible recipients of Zakat.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why Islam encourages Sadaqah?
options: It is intended to increase social rivalry
It promotes generosity and voluntary assistance to others
It is restricted to wealthy Muslims
questions.explanation: Sadaqah is voluntary charity that encourages generosity and assistance to others.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of the Hijrah in Islamic history?
options: It marked the beginning of the Islamic calendar and the establishment of a Muslim community in Madinah
It marked the end of all relations between Muslims and non-Muslims
It was the occasion on which the Qur'an was first revealed
It established Makkah as the first Muslim state
questions.explanation: The Hijrah to Madinah was a major turning point that led to the establishment of the Muslim community and later became the starting point of the Islamic calendar.

questions.text: Which of the following was one of the immediate challenges faced by the Muhajirun after arriving in Madinah?
options: Lack of access to the Ka'bah
Adjustment to a new community and economic circumstances
Absence of any Muslim population in Madinah
questions.explanation: The Muhajirun had left their homes and possessions in Makkah and had to adjust to new social and economic circumstances in Madinah.

questions.text: The Constitution of Madinah was important mainly because it
options: made military service compulsory for every person
provided a framework for relations and responsibilities among different groups in Madinah
restricted residence in Madinah to Muslims alone
questions.explanation: The Constitution of Madinah established principles governing cooperation, responsibilities and relations among the various communities of Madinah.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Battle of Badr?
options: It occurred after the conquest of Makkah
It was fought between Muslims and the Romans
It ended the Prophet's mission in Madinah
It was an important early victory for the Muslims against the Quraysh
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr was a major early confrontation in which the Muslims achieved victory over the Quraysh.

questions.text: What major lesson can Muslims derive from the Battle of Badr?
options: Faith, discipline and reliance on Allah are important in facing difficulties
questions.explanation: Badr demonstrates the importance of faith, discipline, sacrifice and reliance upon Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following was a major cause of the Battle of Khandaq?
options: A dispute over the performance of Hajj
The formation of a coalition against the Muslim community in Madinah
A disagreement among the Ansar concerning inheritance
The refusal of Muslims to migrate to Madinah
questions.explanation: The Battle of Khandaq involved a large coalition that gathered against the Muslim community in Madinah.

questions.text: The strategy of digging a trench around vulnerable parts of Madinah during the Battle of Khandaq demonstrates the importance of
options: using sound strategy while relying upon Allah
questions.explanation: The trench was a strategic defensive measure and shows that Muslims may combine planning and practical means with reliance upon Allah.

questions.text: Which event followed the conquest of Makkah?
options: The Qur'an ceased to be revealed
The obligation of Salah was cancelled
Many former opponents accepted Islam and the idols around the Ka'bah were removed
questions.explanation: After the peaceful conquest of Makkah, many people accepted Islam and the idols associated with polytheism were removed from the Ka'bah.

questions.text: The Prophet's treatment of many former enemies after the conquest of Makkah demonstrates the importance of
questions.explanation: The Prophet demonstrated remarkable mercy and forgiveness toward many former opponents after the conquest.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of the Isra and Mi'raj?
options: It marked the first migration to Abyssinia
It was the miraculous night journey and ascension associated with the Prophet Muhammad
It marked the conquest of Makkah
It was the occasion when Zakah was abolished
questions.explanation: Isra and Mi'raj refers to the miraculous night journey and ascension of the Prophet Muhammad, an event closely associated with the obligation of Salah.

questions.text: Which pillar of Islam is most directly associated with the five daily prayers?
questions.explanation: Salah is the obligatory prayer performed five times daily.

questions.text: Which of the following is a condition that should be fulfilled before performing obligatory Salah?
options: Possessing a large amount of wealth
Observing the prescribed time of the prayer
questions.explanation: Each obligatory prayer has a prescribed time, and performing it within its proper time is an important requirement.

questions.text: What is the significance of facing the Qiblah during Salah?
options: It unites Muslims in a common direction of worship
It makes prayer valid without Wudu
It indicates the social status of the worshipper
It is required only during Hajj
questions.explanation: Facing the Qiblah toward the Ka'bah provides a common direction for Muslims during prayer.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Khushu' in Salah?
options: Reciting the prayer as quickly as possible
Humility, concentration and reverence during prayer
Speaking to other worshippers during prayer
questions.explanation: Khushu' refers to humility, attentiveness and reverence in worship, especially during Salah.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to undermine concentration during Salah?
options: Understanding the meaning of what is recited
Deliberately engaging in unnecessary distractions during prayer
questions.explanation: Unnecessary distractions can weaken concentration and humility during Salah.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the importance of the Adhan?
options: It announces the beginning of Ramadan
It marks the end of Hajj
It announces the time for congregational prayer
questions.explanation: The Adhan is the prescribed call announcing the time for prayer.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the Iqamah?
options: To indicate that the congregational prayer is about to begin
To announce the beginning of Hajj
To announce the death of a Muslim
questions.explanation: The Iqamah is a call indicating that the congregational prayer is ready to begin.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Sujud?
questions.explanation: Sujud is the act of prostration performed during Salah as an expression of submission to Allah.

questions.text: Why is Sujud considered spiritually significant?
options: It removes the need for other forms of worship
It expresses humility and submission to Allah
It is performed only as a cultural tradition
questions.explanation: Prostration is a powerful expression of humility, submission and devotion to Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the role of Dua in Islam?
options: It is permitted only after Hajj
It can replace all obligatory acts
It is a form of supplication through which a Muslim calls upon Allah
questions.explanation: Dua is supplication directed to Allah, through which Muslims ask for guidance, assistance, forgiveness and other lawful needs.

questions.text: Which of the following is most appropriate when making Dua?
options: Demanding that every request must be granted immediately
Using supplication to harm innocent people
questions.explanation: Dua should be made sincerely while relying upon Allah and seeking what is lawful and beneficial.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the concept of Akhirah?
options: The life after death and the final accountability
The migration of Muslims to Abyssinia
questions.explanation: Akhirah refers to the Hereafter, including life after death and accountability before Allah.

questions.text: Belief in the Day of Judgment should encourage a Muslim to
options: act responsibly because deeds will be accounted for
questions.explanation: Belief in accountability encourages Muslims to act responsibly and avoid wrongdoing.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important consequence of belief in accountability before Allah?
options: A person becomes free from all obligations
Worldly success becomes the only goal
A person becomes more conscious of moral choices
questions.explanation: Belief in accountability encourages a person to consider the moral consequences of their actions.

questions.text: Which angel is traditionally associated with conveying Allah's revelation to the prophets?
questions.explanation: Jibril is the angel associated with delivering divine revelation to the prophets.

questions.text: Which of the following is associated with the angel Israfil?
options: Blowing the trumpet in connection with the events of the Last Day
Delivering the Qur'an to every Muslim
questions.explanation: Israfil is traditionally associated with blowing the trumpet at the appointed time connected with the Last Day.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains belief in Allah's angels?
options: Angels possess divine authority equal to Allah
Angels are created beings who carry out tasks assigned to them by Allah
Angels are human beings who became prophets
questions.explanation: Angels are created by Allah and carry out duties according to His command; they are not divine beings.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major distinction between angels and human beings in Islamic belief?
options: Angels require food while humans do not
Humans are always invisible while angels are always visible
Angels are created for obedience to Allah and do not disobey His commands
questions.explanation: Islamic teachings describe angels as beings who obey Allah and carry out the duties assigned to them.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains belief in divine books?
options: Allah revealed guidance to His messengers through scriptures
Every historical book is automatically a divine book
Only books written after the Prophet's death are divine
Divine books were created by ordinary scholars
questions.explanation: Muslims believe that Allah revealed guidance through scriptures given to His messengers.

questions.text: Which of the following scriptures is associated with Prophet Musa?
questions.explanation: The Tawrah is the scripture associated with Prophet Musa.

questions.text: The Zabur is particularly associated with which prophet?
questions.explanation: The Zabur is the scripture associated with Prophet Dawud.

questions.text: The Injil is associated with which prophet?
questions.explanation: The Injil is the scripture associated with Prophet Isa.

questions.text: Which statement best reflects the Islamic position concerning the Qur'an and previous scriptures?
options: The Qur'an confirms the original divine messages and serves as the final revealed scripture
The Qur'an denies that any earlier prophet existed
The Qur'an was revealed only for one tribe
The Qur'an is considered a historical book without religious authority
questions.explanation: Islam teaches that Allah revealed earlier scriptures and that the Qur'an is the final revealed scripture and confirms the essential truth of previous revelation.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major reason Muslims learn Tajwid?
options: To improve the correct pronunciation and recitation of the Qur'an
To replace understanding of the Qur'an
To restrict Qur'anic recitation to scholars
questions.explanation: Tajwid provides rules that help Muslims recite the Qur'an correctly, particularly in pronunciation and articulation.

questions.text: Which of the following is most closely related to Makharij al-Huruf?
options: The points of articulation of Arabic letters
questions.explanation: Makharij al-Huruf refers to the points from which Arabic letters are articulated during recitation.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of observing Tajwid rules when reciting the Qur'an?
options: To make recitation faster than normal speech
To make every reciter use the same voice
To replace memorization of the Qur'an
To preserve correct pronunciation and meaning during recitation
questions.explanation: Tajwid helps preserve correct pronunciation in Qur'anic recitation and protects the intended meaning of the words.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a Sunnah?
options: The teachings, practices and approved ways of the Prophet Muhammad
Any cultural practice found in Arabia
A personal opinion of a modern scholar
A compulsory act that is always equal to Fard
questions.explanation: Sunnah refers to the teachings, practices, actions and approvals of the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.text: Why is the Sunnah important in understanding the Qur'an?
options: It replaces the Qur'an as the primary revelation
It provides practical explanation and demonstration of Qur'anic guidance
It prevents Muslims from studying the Qur'an
It applies only to historical events
questions.explanation: The Sunnah explains and demonstrates how Qur'anic teachings are applied in practice.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Hadith Marfu'?
options: A report attributed only to a later scholar
A report about an ancient king
A report attributed to the Prophet Muhammad
A report whose narrator is unknown
questions.explanation: Hadith Marfu' refers to a report attributed to the Prophet Muhammad, whether concerning his words, actions or approvals.

questions.text: A report attributed directly to a Companion of the Prophet is commonly described as
questions.explanation: A Mawquf report is one attributed to a Companion rather than directly to the Prophet.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Hadith Da'if?
options: A weak Hadith that does not meet the conditions required for an authentic report
A Hadith that is necessarily fabricated
A Hadith found only in the Qur'an
A report whose authenticity is automatically certain
questions.explanation: Hadith Da'if refers to a weak report that does not satisfy the necessary conditions for an authentic Hadith.

questions.text: Why is knowledge of the chain of transmission important in Hadith studies?
options: It determines the age of the Qur'an
It helps scholars investigate how a report was transmitted from one narrator to another
It makes every Hadith automatically authentic
It eliminates the need to examine narrators
questions.explanation: Studying the chain allows scholars to examine the transmission of a report and assess the reliability and continuity of its narrators.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important quality of a trustworthy Hadith narrator?
questions.explanation: Hadith scholars consider the narrator's reliability, uprightness and accuracy when assessing transmissions.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains Ijma?
options: The personal opinion of one scholar
The process of memorizing the Qur'an
The use of Arabic poetry in legal decisions
The agreement of qualified Muslim scholars on a legal issue
questions.explanation: Ijma refers to scholarly consensus on an Islamic legal matter.

questions.text: Why is Ijma important in Islamic jurisprudence?
options: It can provide authoritative guidance on matters requiring scholarly agreement
It allows every person to create new religious obligations
It applies only to matters of Arabic pronunciation
questions.explanation: Ijma provides a recognized basis for legal guidance where qualified scholars reach agreement on a matter.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains Maslahah in Islamic legal reasoning?
options: Consideration of public benefit and welfare within Islamic principles
Rejection of all established legal principles
Preference for one's relatives in legal matters
questions.explanation: Maslahah involves considering public benefit and welfare in accordance with the objectives and principles of Islamic law.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important objective of Islamic law?
options: Protecting essential human interests and promoting justice
Giving unlimited authority to wealthy individuals
questions.explanation: Islamic law aims to protect essential human interests, promote justice and establish beneficial social order.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates the principle of consultation in community affairs?
options: A leader making every decision secretly
A ruler refusing to hear qualified advice
A wealthy person controlling all decisions
A leader seeking appropriate advice before making an important decision
questions.explanation: Consultation, or Shura, involves seeking appropriate advice and considering relevant views in important communal matters.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major responsibility of a Muslim leader?
options: To protect people's rights and administer justice
To favour relatives in every decision
To use public resources for personal benefit
questions.explanation: Islamic leadership involves responsibility, justice, protection of rights and proper management of entrusted affairs.

questions.text: Which of the following actions by a public official constitutes a breach of Amanah?
options: Using entrusted public funds for personal purposes
questions.explanation: Using public resources for personal purposes violates the trust placed in a public official.

questions.text: Which of the following best demonstrates Islamic environmental responsibility?
options: Wasting water because it is inexpensive
Avoiding unnecessary waste and protecting useful resources
questions.explanation: Islam encourages responsible use of resources and discourages waste, harm and unnecessary destruction.

questions.text: Which of the following best reflects Islamic teaching on seeking knowledge?
options: Knowledge should be restricted to rulers
Only religious knowledge has any value
Knowledge should be used mainly to gain social status
Beneficial knowledge should be pursued and used responsibly
questions.explanation: Islam encourages the pursuit of beneficial knowledge and responsible use of what is learned.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of the Hijrah in Islamic history?
options: It marked the beginning of the Islamic calendar and the establishment of a Muslim community in Madinah
It marked the end of all relations between Muslims and non-Muslims
It was the occasion on which the Qur'an was first revealed
It established Makkah as the first Muslim state
questions.explanation: The Hijrah to Madinah was a major turning point that led to the establishment of the Muslim community and later became the starting point of the Islamic calendar.

questions.text: Which of the following was one of the immediate challenges faced by the Muhajirun after arriving in Madinah?
options: Lack of access to the Ka'bah
Adjustment to a new community and economic circumstances
Absence of any Muslim population in Madinah
questions.explanation: The Muhajirun had left their homes and possessions in Makkah and had to adjust to new social and economic circumstances in Madinah.

questions.text: The Constitution of Madinah was important mainly because it
options: made military service compulsory for every person
provided a framework for relations and responsibilities among different groups in Madinah
restricted residence in Madinah to Muslims alone
questions.explanation: The Constitution of Madinah established principles governing cooperation, responsibilities and relations among the various communities of Madinah.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Battle of Badr?
options: It occurred after the conquest of Makkah
It was fought between Muslims and the Romans
It ended the Prophet's mission in Madinah
It was an important early victory for the Muslims against the Quraysh
questions.explanation: The Battle of Badr was a major early confrontation in which the Muslims achieved victory over the Quraysh.

questions.text: What major lesson can Muslims derive from the Battle of Badr?
options: Faith, discipline and reliance on Allah are important in facing difficulties
questions.explanation: Badr demonstrates the importance of faith, discipline, sacrifice and reliance upon Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following was a major cause of the Battle of Khandaq?
options: A dispute over the performance of Hajj
The formation of a coalition against the Muslim community in Madinah
A disagreement among the Ansar concerning inheritance
The refusal of Muslims to migrate to Madinah
questions.explanation: The Battle of Khandaq involved a large coalition that gathered against the Muslim community in Madinah.

questions.text: The strategy of digging a trench around vulnerable parts of Madinah during the Battle of Khandaq demonstrates the importance of
options: using sound strategy while relying upon Allah
questions.explanation: The trench was a strategic defensive measure and shows that Muslims may combine planning and practical means with reliance upon Allah.

questions.text: Which event followed the conquest of Makkah?
options: The Qur'an ceased to be revealed
The obligation of Salah was cancelled
Many former opponents accepted Islam and the idols around the Ka'bah were removed
questions.explanation: After the peaceful conquest of Makkah, many people accepted Islam and the idols associated with polytheism were removed from the Ka'bah.

questions.text: The Prophet's treatment of many former enemies after the conquest of Makkah demonstrates the importance of
questions.explanation: The Prophet demonstrated remarkable mercy and forgiveness toward many former opponents after the conquest.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of the Isra and Mi'raj?
options: It marked the first migration to Abyssinia
It was the miraculous night journey and ascension associated with the Prophet Muhammad
It marked the conquest of Makkah
It was the occasion when Zakah was abolished
questions.explanation: Isra and Mi'raj refers to the miraculous night journey and ascension of the Prophet Muhammad, an event closely associated with the obligation of Salah.

questions.text: Which pillar of Islam is most directly associated with the five daily prayers?
questions.explanation: Salah is the obligatory prayer performed five times daily.

questions.text: Which of the following is a condition that should be fulfilled before performing obligatory Salah?
options: Possessing a large amount of wealth
Observing the prescribed time of the prayer
questions.explanation: Each obligatory prayer has a prescribed time, and performing it within its proper time is an important requirement.

questions.text: What is the significance of facing the Qiblah during Salah?
options: It unites Muslims in a common direction of worship
It makes prayer valid without Wudu
It indicates the social status of the worshipper
It is required only during Hajj
questions.explanation: Facing the Qiblah toward the Ka'bah provides a common direction for Muslims during prayer.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Khushu' in Salah?
options: Reciting the prayer as quickly as possible
Humility, concentration and reverence during prayer
Speaking to other worshippers during prayer
questions.explanation: Khushu' refers to humility, attentiveness and reverence in worship, especially during Salah.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to undermine concentration during Salah?
options: Understanding the meaning of what is recited
Deliberately engaging in unnecessary distractions during prayer
questions.explanation: Unnecessary distractions can weaken concentration and humility during Salah.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the importance of the Adhan?
options: It announces the beginning of Ramadan
It marks the end of Hajj
It announces the time for congregational prayer
questions.explanation: The Adhan is the prescribed call announcing the time for prayer.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the Iqamah?
options: To indicate that the congregational prayer is about to begin
To announce the beginning of Hajj
To announce the death of a Muslim
questions.explanation: The Iqamah is a call indicating that the congregational prayer is ready to begin.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Sujud?
questions.explanation: Sujud is the act of prostration performed during Salah as an expression of submission to Allah.

questions.text: Why is Sujud considered spiritually significant?
options: It removes the need for other forms of worship
It expresses humility and submission to Allah
It is performed only as a cultural tradition
questions.explanation: Prostration is a powerful expression of humility, submission and devotion to Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the role of Dua in Islam?
options: It is permitted only after Hajj
It can replace all obligatory acts
It is a form of supplication through which a Muslim calls upon Allah
questions.explanation: Dua is supplication directed to Allah, through which Muslims ask for guidance, assistance, forgiveness and other lawful needs.

questions.text: Which of the following is most appropriate when making Dua?
options: Demanding that every request must be granted immediately
Using supplication to harm innocent people
questions.explanation: Dua should be made sincerely while relying upon Allah and seeking what is lawful and beneficial.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the concept of Akhirah?
options: The life after death and the final accountability
The migration of Muslims to Abyssinia
questions.explanation: Akhirah refers to the Hereafter, including life after death and accountability before Allah.

questions.text: Belief in the Day of Judgment should encourage a Muslim to
options: act responsibly because deeds will be accounted for
questions.explanation: Belief in accountability encourages Muslims to act responsibly and avoid wrongdoing.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important consequence of belief in accountability before Allah?
options: A person becomes free from all obligations
Worldly success becomes the only goal
A person becomes more conscious of moral choices
questions.explanation: Belief in accountability encourages a person to consider the moral consequences of their actions.

questions.text: Which angel is traditionally associated with conveying Allah's revelation to the prophets?
questions.explanation: Jibril is the angel associated with delivering divine revelation to the prophets.

questions.text: Which of the following is associated with the angel Israfil?
options: Blowing the trumpet in connection with the events of the Last Day
Delivering the Qur'an to every Muslim
questions.explanation: Israfil is traditionally associated with blowing the trumpet at the appointed time connected with the Last Day.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains belief in Allah's angels?
options: Angels possess divine authority equal to Allah
Angels are created beings who carry out tasks assigned to them by Allah
Angels are human beings who became prophets
questions.explanation: Angels are created by Allah and carry out duties according to His command; they are not divine beings.

Avoiding unnecessary waste and protecting useful resources
