questions.text: Which of the following was one of the major reasons the Quraysh opposed the Prophet Muhammad's message in Makkah?
options: The message challenged their religious practices and established interests
The Prophet prevented them from learning Arabic
The message required them to migrate to Abyssinia
The Prophet abolished all forms of trade
questions.explanation: The Quraysh opposed Islam partly because the message of Tawhid challenged their polytheistic beliefs and established social and economic interests.

questions.text: Which of the following was a major method used by the Quraysh to discourage people from accepting Islam?
options: Persecuting and threatening those who accepted Islam
Inviting all Muslims to govern Makkah
questions.explanation: The Quraysh used various forms of persecution, intimidation and social pressure against early Muslims.

questions.text: The boycott imposed on the Prophet's clan and their supporters demonstrated the Quraysh's attempt to
options: encourage Muslims to migrate to Madinah
isolate the Prophet and weaken support for his mission
establish peaceful relations with the Muslims
questions.explanation: The boycott was intended to place social and economic pressure on the Prophet, his clan and their supporters.

questions.text: Which event is commonly known as the Year of Sorrow?
options: The year of the conquest of Makkah
The year of the Battle of Badr
The year of the first revelation
The period in which Khadijah and Abu Talib died
questions.explanation: The Year of Sorrow refers to the period when the Prophet lost his wife Khadijah and his uncle Abu Talib.

questions.text: What major support did Abu Talib provide to the Prophet Muhammad during the Makkan period?
options: He offered protection and support despite not accepting Islam
He led the first Muslim army in Madinah
He compiled the Qur'an into one book
He negotiated the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
questions.explanation: Abu Talib provided important protection and social support to the Prophet during the difficult Makkan period.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the importance of Khadijah (RA) to the early Islamic mission?
options: She led the army at Badr
She gave the Prophet emotional and material support during the early mission
She became the first ruler of Madinah
questions.explanation: Khadijah strongly supported the Prophet emotionally and materially, particularly during the difficult early years of revelation.

questions.text: Who was among the earliest people to accept the Prophet Muhammad's message?
questions.explanation: Khadijah was the first person to accept the Prophet Muhammad's message.

questions.text: Which companion was particularly known for freeing and supporting persecuted Muslim slaves during the Makkan period?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr used his wealth to purchase and free several persecuted slaves, including Bilal.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates the significance of Bilal ibn Rabah's experience in Makkah?
options: It demonstrates steadfastness in faith despite severe persecution
It demonstrates the superiority of wealthy Muslims
It shows that Islam was restricted to Arabs
It proves that early Muslims avoided all forms of hardship
questions.explanation: Bilal's perseverance despite persecution illustrates steadfastness and commitment to Islamic faith.

questions.text: The conversion of Umar ibn al-Khattab was significant because it
options: ended the revelation of the Qur'an
strengthened the confidence and position of the Muslims in Makkah
caused the Muslims to leave Arabia immediately
resulted in the abolition of Salah
questions.explanation: Umar's acceptance of Islam strengthened the Muslims because of his courage, social position and public support for the faith.

questions.text: Which of the following was a significant feature of the Prophet's preaching in the early Makkan period?
options: It focused mainly on military administration
It emphasized Tawhid, accountability and moral reform
It established detailed rules of international diplomacy
questions.explanation: The early Makkan message strongly emphasized monotheism, resurrection, accountability and moral reform.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why the Prophet initially preached to close relatives and selected individuals?
options: Islam was intended only for relatives
The Prophet was forbidden from speaking publicly
The Qur'an had not yet been revealed
The early mission developed gradually before becoming more public
questions.explanation: The Prophet's mission initially developed gradually among close contacts before public preaching became more prominent.

questions.text: Which of the following is an important lesson from the patience of early Muslims in Makkah?
options: Believers should remain steadfast when facing legitimate hardship
Material success is the only measure of faith
Religious commitment is unnecessary during difficulty
questions.explanation: The early Muslims demonstrated patience and steadfastness while facing serious persecution and hardship.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the significance of the first migration to Abyssinia?
options: It was the first military expedition of Islam
It demonstrated that Muslims could seek safety under a just non-Muslim ruler
It marked the conquest of Ethiopia
It established Madinah as the capital
questions.explanation: The migration to Abyssinia showed that Muslims could seek protection under a just ruler outside Arabia.

questions.text: The ruler of Abyssinia who provided protection to the Muslim migrants was known as
questions.explanation: The ruler of Abyssinia was known as the Negus, or Najashi, and he provided protection to the Muslim migrants.

questions.text: Which quality of the Negus was particularly appreciated by the Muslim migrants?
questions.explanation: The Negus was regarded as a just ruler who gave the Muslim migrants protection.

questions.text: Which of the following was one of the outcomes of the First Pledge of Aqabah?
options: People from Yathrib pledged to uphold basic Islamic principles
The Ka'bah was moved to Madinah
The Battle of Uhud was fought
questions.explanation: The First Pledge of Aqabah involved people from Yathrib accepting Islamic teachings and pledging to uphold them.

questions.text: The Second Pledge of Aqabah was particularly important because it involved
options: a stronger commitment to support and protect the Prophet
the establishment of the first Islamic university
questions.explanation: The Second Pledge included a stronger commitment from people of Yathrib to support and protect the Prophet.

questions.text: Which city was known as Yathrib before it became widely known as Madinah?
questions.explanation: Yathrib was the earlier name of the city that became known as Madinah.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the term Muhajirun?
options: Muslims who lived permanently in Makkah
Residents of Abyssinia who accepted Islam
The people of Madinah who welcomed the Prophet
Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madinah
questions.explanation: Muhajirun refers to the Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madinah for the sake of their faith.

questions.text: The Ansar were mainly
options: Muslims of Madinah who supported and welcomed the migrants
questions.explanation: The Ansar were Muslims from Madinah who welcomed, supported and assisted the Muhajirun.

questions.text: Which of the following best demonstrates the spirit of the Ansar?
options: Sharing resources and providing support to the Muhajirun
Demanding that migrants return to Makkah
questions.explanation: The Ansar demonstrated generosity and brotherhood by supporting the Muhajirun and helping them settle in Madinah.

questions.text: Which companion served as a guide for the Prophet and Abu Bakr during the Hijrah?
questions.explanation: Abdullah ibn Uraiqit acted as a guide during the Prophet's migration journey to Madinah.

questions.text: The Prophet's stay in the cave during the Hijrah demonstrates the importance of
options: careful planning together with trust in Allah
questions.explanation: The Hijrah involved careful planning and practical measures while maintaining trust in Allah.

questions.text: Which mosque is traditionally associated with the Prophet's first stop after leaving Makkah for Madinah?
questions.explanation: Masjid Quba is associated with the Prophet's arrival near Madinah during the Hijrah and is traditionally regarded as the first mosque established by the Prophet in Madinah.

questions.text: What was one major function of the Prophet's mosque in Madinah?
options: It served only as a place for private prayer
It served as a centre for worship, learning and community affairs
It was used exclusively for military training
It was reserved for wealthy Muslims
questions.explanation: The Prophet's mosque served multiple functions, including worship, education, consultation and community administration.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the significance of the Suffah in Madinah?
options: It was a marketplace for Quraysh merchants
It was a military fort outside Makkah
It was associated with learning and the support of needy companions
It was the residence of foreign rulers
questions.explanation: The Suffah was an area associated with companions who devoted themselves to learning and worship and who often required communal support.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates the Prophet's educational method?
options: Using explanation, demonstration, questions and practical examples
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught through various methods, including explanation, demonstration, questioning and practical examples.

questions.text: Why did the Prophet encourage his companions to memorize the Qur'an?
options: To preserve and transmit the revealed guidance accurately
To prevent the Qur'an from being understood
To replace all written records permanently
To restrict knowledge to a few individuals
questions.explanation: Memorization helped preserve the Qur'an and enabled its accurate transmission among the Muslim community.

questions.text: Which of the following contributed significantly to the preservation of the Qur'an during the Prophet's lifetime?
options: The use of foreign translations only
Memorization and written recording of revealed verses
The prohibition of teaching the Qur'an
questions.explanation: The Qur'an was preserved through memorization by companions and written recording of revealed passages.

questions.text: Who played a major role in compiling the Qur'an into a collected manuscript during the caliphate of Abu Bakr?
questions.explanation: Zayd ibn Thabit was entrusted with the important task of collecting the Qur'anic material into a compiled manuscript during Abu Bakr's caliphate.

questions.text: Why was the compilation of the Qur'an undertaken during Abu Bakr's caliphate?
options: To change the wording of the Qur'an
To preserve the Qur'anic text in a collected form after the deaths of many memorizers
questions.explanation: The deaths of many Qur'an memorizers in battles created concern about preservation, leading to the collection of the Qur'anic material into a manuscript.

questions.text: What was one major objective of Uthman's standardization of Qur'anic copies?
options: To reduce disputes arising from differences in recitation and written copies
To remove verses from the Qur'an
To translate the Qur'an into every language
To prevent Muslims from memorizing the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Uthman standardized copies of the Qur'anic text to help preserve unity and reduce disputes arising from differences in written forms and recitation.

questions.text: Which companion was appointed by Abu Bakr to lead the collection of the Qur'anic material?
questions.explanation: Zayd ibn Thabit was appointed to undertake the collection of Qur'anic material during Abu Bakr's caliphate.

questions.text: Which of the following was one of the major achievements of Abu Bakr's caliphate?
options: Building the first university in Baghdad
Preserving the unity of the Muslim community after the Prophet's death
Moving the capital permanently to Egypt
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr played a crucial role in maintaining the unity of the Muslim community during the difficult period following the Prophet's death.

questions.text: Which challenge confronted Abu Bakr soon after becoming caliph?
options: Rebellion and refusal by some groups to fulfil their obligations to the Muslim community
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr faced rebellions, false claimants to prophethood and opposition to obligations such as Zakah.

questions.text: Which quality of Abu Bakr was especially important in dealing with the challenges after the Prophet's death?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr demonstrated firmness and determination in preserving the unity and religious obligations of the Muslim community.

questions.text: Which of the following is associated with the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab?
options: The first revelation to Prophet Muhammad
Significant expansion and administrative development of the Muslim state
The migration from Makkah to Madinah
questions.explanation: Umar's caliphate witnessed major territorial expansion as well as important administrative and institutional developments.

questions.text: Which of the following qualities is strongly associated with Umar ibn al-Khattab's leadership?
questions.explanation: Umar was well known for his strong concern for justice, accountability and the welfare of the people.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates Umar's concern for public welfare?
options: Ignoring the needs of the poor
Giving all public resources to his relatives
Establishing systems to organize public administration and support social welfare
questions.explanation: Umar developed administrative systems and paid close attention to the welfare and needs of the Muslim population.

questions.text: Which of the following is associated with the caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan?
options: The standardization and distribution of official Qur'anic copies
The first revelation in Cave Hira
The construction of the Ka'bah by Ibrahim
questions.explanation: Uthman is particularly associated with standardizing and distributing official copies of the Qur'anic text.

questions.text: Which quality of Uthman ibn Affan was particularly noted among his companions?
options: Refusal to support the Muslim community
questions.explanation: Uthman was well known for generosity, modesty and significant financial support for the Muslim community.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes Ali ibn Abi Talib's relationship with the Prophet Muhammad?
options: He was a Quraysh opponent who never accepted Islam
He was the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law and an early Muslim
He was the ruler of Abyssinia
questions.explanation: Ali was the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law and was among the earliest people to accept Islam.

questions.text: Which quality of Ali ibn Abi Talib is frequently emphasized in Islamic history?
options: Knowledge, courage and devotion to Islam
questions.explanation: Ali is widely remembered for his knowledge, courage and strong commitment to Islam.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Rightly Guided Caliphs?
options: They were the four early caliphs who succeeded the Prophet and are traditionally regarded as exemplary leaders
They were rulers of the Roman Empire
They were all prophets after Muhammad
They were governors appointed by the Quraysh before Islam
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali are known as the Rightly Guided Caliphs because of their early leadership of the Muslim community.

questions.text: Which principle can be learned from the leadership of the Rightly Guided Caliphs?
options: Leadership should be based solely on wealth
Leadership involves responsibility, justice and accountability
Public resources belong personally to the ruler
questions.explanation: The leadership of the Rightly Guided Caliphs illustrates responsibility, justice, consultation and accountability.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Islamic concept of Shirk?
options: Associating partners with Allah in worship or divinity
questions.explanation: Shirk means associating partners with Allah in worship, divinity or attributes that belong uniquely to Him.

questions.text: Why is Shirk regarded as a serious violation of Tawhid?
options: It prevents people from engaging in trade
It contradicts the belief that Allah alone deserves worship
questions.explanation: Shirk contradicts Tawhid because it gives worship or divine status to beings or things besides Allah.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates sincerity in worship?
options: Performing an act of worship primarily to please Allah
Giving charity only to receive praise
Praying only when people are watching
questions.explanation: Sincerity means directing worship to Allah and seeking His pleasure rather than people's admiration.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to strengthen Ikhlas?
options: Focusing on Allah's acceptance rather than people's approval
Comparing one's worship with that of others
questions.explanation: Ikhlas is strengthened when a Muslim focuses on Allah's pleasure rather than seeking recognition from people.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the Islamic meaning of Akhlaq?
questions.explanation: Akhlaq refers to moral character, manners and conduct.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of good Akhlaq?
options: Mocking people because of their weaknesses
Speaking respectfully and treating others with kindness
questions.explanation: Respectful speech, kindness and good treatment of others are examples of good Islamic character.

questions.text: Which of the following best demonstrates Wafa' al-Ahd?
options: Fulfilling a legitimate promise or agreement
Hiding important information from a partner
questions.explanation: Wafa' al-Ahd means fulfilling promises, covenants and legitimate agreements.
